🇩🇪 Deutsch · 🇬🇧 English 

 Open-source alternative to Notion and Confluence – documents, databases, whiteboards and a daily journal for teams, self-hosted in one container or hosted in Germany.

 Demo · Docs · Install

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 

Website · Hosted version · Discord · Changelog

 

 Contents

- At a glance
- Quick start · Deploy
- Features · Screenshots · How Flowplan compares · Private by design
- A closer look: Write · Databases · AI · Whiteboards and journal · Handwriting · Home page · Together
- For admins and integrations: architecture, system requirements, security
- FAQ
- Development
- Community: help translate, contributors, star history
- Support Flowplan

 At a glance

- Everything in one page tree – documents, databases with ten views, whiteboards, notebooks for handwriting, a daily journal, projects with tickets and sprints, surveys and workflows.
- Completely open source under the AGPL-3.0 – no closed enterprise edition, no features behind a licence key.
- One container with SQLite – nothing else to run, no external search service. For larger teams optionally PostgreSQL and a cluster of several instances. Or hosted in Germany at app.flowplan.org.
- Optional AI – off by default; admins switch it on per feature and per person, completely local with Ollama or with a key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service. You decide which pages it may read.
- Private by design – no tracking, permissions down to a single record, two-factor sign-in, encryption of files and backups with your own key.
- Your data stays portable – Markdown with frontmatter, CSV and ZIP, scheduled exports to S3 or Git, import from Notion, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Jira and Trello.

The interface is available in German, English, French and Simplified Chinese – further languages can be added as JSON catalogues (help translate); the documentation is in English and German.

 Quick start

Try Flowplan on your own computer with a single command:

 

Open and choose Create account – the first account administers the instance. APP URL must be the address exactly as you type it in the browser: to reach Flowplan from another device or under a domain, change it (for example -e APP URL= and put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front. All data lives in the flowplan volume.

 
 Docker Compose for a server – volume, APP URL and optional S3 

 

 docker compose up -d , then open your domain. Single sign-on, e-mail and every other setting are environment variables too – see Configuration.

 

The repository also has a ready-made compose.yaml with an example configuration:

 

- Local AI (optional): docker compose --profile ai up -d starts Ollama next to Flowplan; set OLLAMA URL= and choose a model under Administration → AI (AI).
- Kubernetes: the Helm chart in deploy/helm/flowplan (one pod with a volume, as SQLite needs; several pods in cluster mode).
- Single sign-on: register a confidential web client at your OIDC provider with the redirect URI https:// /api/auth/callback (Sign-in).

- Larger teams: instead of SQLite, Flowplan can use PostgreSQL (with pgvector for semantic search) – and with PostgreSQL, Redis and S3, several instances behind a load balancer in cluster mode. An existing instance switches between SQLite and PostgreSQL in both directions; Sizing says which setup fits how many people.

All data lives in the volume on /app/data . With SQLite, run exactly one container per data directory.

 
 Images and automatic deployment 

The image is published to the GitHub Container Registry for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 :

 

Images are built only for a release or by hand: Actions → Docker image → Run workflow builds :beta from the chosen branch (with a version, it rebuilds that release instead). Every :beta image can be rolled out on Coolify automatically: set the repository secrets COOLIFY WEBHOOK (the resource's deploy webhook) and COOLIFY TOKEN (an API token with deploy permission), and let the Coolify resource use the :beta image. A release that is newer than the current :beta (its commit not yet contained in it) is tagged :beta as well and rolled out the same way; an older release leaves it alone. See Coolify and reverse proxies.

 

More in the documentation: Installation · Configuration · Storage, S3 and backups · Operations

 Deploy

One click to a running instance with your own address – or one command on any server:

 
 

 

- Render ( render.yaml ): the image with a persistent disk on /app/data – disks need a paid instance (Starter or larger); the address is the onrender.com one until you set APP URL to your domain.
- DigitalOcean App Platform ( .do/deploy.template.yaml ): no volumes there, so the data goes to a PostgreSQL database and uploads need a Spaces bucket ( S3 ) – without it, files are lost on every deploy; the dev database has no backups.
- Any server with Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12 (Hetzner, Netcup, IONOS …): paste deploy/cloud-init.yaml as "user data" when creating the server (set FLOWPLAN DOMAIN= in it), or run the command above on an existing one – Docker, Caddy with HTTPS, generated secrets, firewall; the data stays in a Docker volume on the server.

Step by step: Deploy in one click.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Try Flowplan on your own computer with a single command:

docker run -d --name flowplan -p 3000:3000 -v flowplan:/app/data -e APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest

Open http://localhost:3000 and choose Create account – the first account administers the instance. APP_URL must be the address exactly as you type it in the browser: to reach Flowplan from another device or under a domain, change it (for example -e APP_URL=https://flowplan.example.com) and put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front. All data lives in the flowplan volume.

Docker Compose for a server – volume, APP_URL and optional S3
services:
  flowplan:
    image: ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3000:3000"   # a reverse proxy with HTTPS sits in front
    environment:
      APP_URL: https://flowplan.example.com
      # Recommended: the first account only via https://flowplan.example.com/register?setup=<token>
      # (openssl rand -hex 24), so nobody sets the instance up before you
      # FLOWPLAN_SETUP_TOKEN: ...
      # Optional: mirror files to S3 and back up the database continuously (Litestream)
      # S3_BUCKET: flowplan
      # S3_ENDPOINT: https://s3.example.com
      # S3_REGION: eu-central-1
      # S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ...
      # S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ...
      # Encrypts files in the bucket, backups and exports: openssl rand -base64 32
      # FLOWPLAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ...
    volumes:
      - flowplan-data:/app/data

volumes:
  flowplan-data:

docker compose up -d, then open your domain. Single sign-on, e-mail and every other setting are environment variables too – see Configuration.

The repository also has a ready-made compose.yaml with an example configuration:

curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/compose.yaml
curl -o .env https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannicschuller/flowplan/main/.env.example
# edit .env: at least APP_URL (optionally OIDC_* and SMTP_*)
docker compose up -d

  • Local AI (optional): docker compose --profile ai up -d starts Ollama next to Flowplan; set OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434 and choose a model under Administration → AI (AI).

  • Kubernetes: the Helm chart in deploy/helm/flowplan (one pod with a volume, as SQLite needs; several pods in cluster mode).

  • Single sign-on: register a confidential web client at your OIDC provider with the redirect URI https://<your-domain>/api/auth/callback (Sign-in).

  • Larger teams: instead of SQLite, Flowplan can use PostgreSQL (with pgvector for semantic search) – and with PostgreSQL, Redis and S3, several instances behind a load balancer in cluster mode. An existing instance switches between SQLite and PostgreSQL in both directions; Sizing says which setup fits how many people.

All data lives in the volume on /app/data. With SQLite, run exactly one container per data directory.

Images and automatic deployment

The image is published to the GitHub Container Registry for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64:

ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:latest     # the latest release
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:1.2.3      # a fixed release (also :1.2 and :1)
ghcr.io/yannicschuller/flowplan:beta       # the latest manual build, not for production

Images are built only for a release or by hand: Actions → Docker image → Run workflow builds :beta from the chosen branch (with a version, it rebuilds that release instead). Every :beta image can be rolled out on Coolify automatically: set the repository secrets COOLIFY_WEBHOOK (the resource's deploy webhook) and COOLIFY_TOKEN (an API token with deploy permission), and let the Coolify resource use the :beta image. A release that is newer than the current :beta (its commit not yet contained in it) is tagged :beta as well and rolled out the same way; an older release leaves it alone. See Coolify and reverse proxies.

More in the documentation: Installation · Configuration · Storage, S3 and backups · Operations

features.title: Features
features.html:
📝 Documents
A block editor with the / menu, Markdown shortcuts, formulas, Mermaid, footnotes and version history.		 🗂️ Databases and views
23 property types with relations and formulas – as table, board, calendar, timeline, gallery, chart and more.		 🧩 Whiteboards
Sticky notes, connectors, mind maps and shape libraries – and server racks with cabling.
📔 Journal
One page per day with templates, trackers, monthly reviews and an optional PIN lock.		 🎯 Projects and sprints
Tickets like WEB-123, epics, sprints with burndown, automations and a Git connection.		 📋 Forms and surveys
Forms on any database and surveys with 19 question types – every answer is a record.
🔎 Collections and search
Full-text search with OCR for PDFs and Office files; keep searches and filters as collections.		 ✨ AI, optional
Off until an admin turns it on – locally with Ollama or with your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini key.		 🔄 Import and export
In from Notion, Confluence, AFFiNE, AppFlowy, Obsidian, Evernote and more; out as Markdown, CSV, PDF or Word.
📱 Apps
An installable web app that works offline, desktop apps, and apps for iPhone, iPad and Android.		 🔐 Security
SSO with OIDC, LDAP and SCIM, two-factor sign-in, passkeys and end-to-end encrypted spaces.		 💾 Self-hosting and backups
One container with SQLite or PostgreSQL and a cluster, continuous backup to S3 with Litestream, scheduled encrypted backups, a Helm chart.
🔀 Workflows
Flows of nodes on a canvas, without code: a trigger – a record, page, form, schedule, mention, webhook or e-mail – then conditions, loops, waits and approvals, and actions on records and pages, notifications, AI and HTTP. Test runs, run history, versions, templates and an AI builder; a workflow never does more than the person who activated it.
